##### DANGs

DANGs encode the structure of the causal process within individuals separately from the structure of the causal process across individuals.  The former is termed the *structural part* of the DANG and the latter the *relational part*.  The relational part shows which pairs of observational units influence each other.  For instance, in @fig-causal-dang-instructions we see that individuals 1 and 2 are related.

The structural part is a DAG of vector-valued variables whose length equals the number of observational units in the sample.  It has the standard interpretation under [d-separation rules](#sec-d-separation): it gives the conditional independencies across these vector-valued random variables. For instance, below is a DANG of the model we developed for [Example 2](#sec-example-2).

The structural part is a DAG of vector-valued variables $\mathbf{L}$, $\mathbf{A}$, and $\mathbf{Y}$ of length equal to the number of people in the sample. It shows the relationship between units 1 and 2 separately from the causal structure linking employment, dress, and job opportunities.
